statement: The bridge status language distinguishes preserved, reduced, refuted, absorbed, named blocker, higher-support escape, and not-applicable outcomes.
Delete-redundant status is classified as reduced to smaller witness under redundancy precondition.
Project-to-active status is classified as preserved, reduced, named blocker, or deferred escape using the status skeleton.
Coordinate contraction status is classified as preserved/reduced if equivalent-coordinate congruence holds, otherwise named operation blocker.
Canonical compression status is classified as reduced-to-smaller-witness if motif rewrite preserves/reduces status, otherwise named operation blocker.
Family-chain absorption status is classified as refuted, absorbed, reduced, named blocker, or higher-support escape.
Frontier capture is named as downstream support<=8 limited-theorem input after valid reduction.
Tail obstruction is named as checked support8 tail capture after valid reduction.
Irreducible support>8 status failure is named as higher-support escape, not closed.

statement: Any status_reduced_to_smaller_witness claim requires strict selected support/canonical measure decrease.
Any status_refuted_by_contradiction claim requires a valid contradiction tied to the same payload/status branch.
Named operation blockers, higher-support escapes, not-applicable operations, and successful reductions are disjoint classes.
Every selected operation status branch is preserved, reduced, refuted, absorbed, named blocker, higher-support escape, or not applicable.
